explicit_propositions.text: FOMO is the fear of missing out on exciting or interesting events occurring elsewhere.
Social media frequently triggers FOMO by showcasing curated highlights of others' lives.
People tend to post only positive experiences on social media, omitting struggles or failures.
The speaker experienced FOMO when friends returned from a trip to Seattle without including him.
FOMO arises from unmet needs to feel loved, significant, and connected.
Self-love and self-contentment reduce the intensity of FOMO.
Living vicariously through others’ lives leads to missing out on one’s own present experiences.
Gratitude practices, such as listing three daily gratitudes, help diminish FOMO.
Opportunity cost exists—every decision involves sacrificing alternative possibilities.
A healthy form of FOMO can motivate meaningful action, such as strengthening relationships or pursuing growth.
